punchline: Galton found that children drift back toward the average height.
thirty_sec: In 1886 Francis Galton studied 930 adult children from 205 parentages. Their height-deviate was, on average, two-thirds of the mid-parent's, so very tall parents had less tall children and very short parents had less short ones. He called it regression towards mediocrity.
question: Which recent extreme result did you explain by your own action when it may have moved back to normal?
key_contrast: Extremes tend to drift back toward the average.
